`ignore` is small on purpose. An entry lists exact literals — matched as
written, so `tag` never covers `tags` — and the file prefixes they apply
to. It is for words a block happens to share with vault syntax or with a
storage format, never for a reference someone would rather not fix.
`allowed` is a GRANDFATHER LIST, not a design. A key is `<path> -> <block>`,
or `<path> -> *` when a file names every block at once. Every entry
carries the issue that tracks removing it; an entry without one is not an
exception, it is an unrecorded violation. Entries come off as the code is
touched, and the gate warns about one that no longer matches anything.

why: `#tag` is vault syntax: an AST node kind on the wire and a CodeMirror
decoration in the editor core, both of which must keep working with
every block switched off. The tags BLOCK is the tag pane and tag page
in ui/src/tags, which these files neither import nor name.

.md must stay correct either way. It is substrate for the same reason
block ids are. What the block owns is RESOLVING a reference to a value,

reason: The plugin registry is the list of blocks: `Feature` has a variant, an
id and a settings key per block, so adding one edits plumbing and
removing one leaves a dead variant. This is the Rust half of what
ui/src/shell/registerBlocks.ts already does properly — the shell should
hand the engine its registrations, so the census and the registry stop
being two lists of the same thing.
